extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society / natural philosophers and experimentalists (17th-century scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for describing, performing, and reporting experimental natural-philosophy investigations (mechanical contrivances, chemical/technical processes, natural history observations, and geographic measurements) as in a Royal Society/Philosophical Transactions paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and operation of Papin's water-raising contrivance
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed mechanical arrangement: a great tumbler AA with a small hole in the bottom communicating by a slender pipe ILL with a well-shut pump or bellows MM; a slender pipe NN connecting glass AA with the crown FF; a hollow, bottom-shut coral EE open at the top with crooked outlet pipes DD; concealed pipe OO passing through the coral bottom toward the rock CC; a conveyance pipe PP from glass GG into rock CC with valve Q to prevent return; and a valve R at the top of OO to prevent fall back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the pneumatic principle (rarefying and restoring air to drive circulation): opening bellows MM rarefies crown FF and rock CC, driving water up through OO and into the coral EE and DD; shutting MM forces air back into AA and presses water into rock CC via PP. Practical construction notes: small holes, well-soldered joints, valves to prevent backflow. Advantage noted over ordinary pumps: motive power may be taken far from the water (e.g., river stream driving an axis), and arrangement of multiple receptacles/bellows allows raising water to considerable height.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple receptacles and alternating bellows for continuous lift
rubrics_metrics.description: Several receptacles (AB, AB, etc.) set above one another, each well shut and soldered, connected in pairs to two pumps (HH and II) by slender pipes (CDD, EFF); pumps are moved by an axis LL so that when one descends the other ascends; valves (O, Q, etc.) fitted to top of ascending pipes to prevent water descent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational prescription: arrange bellows/pumps alternately (first open, second shut, third open, etc.) so lower receptacle supplies the next, raising water stepwise. Use a wheel MM on the axis LL driven by a river stream to automate motion. Emphasises correct piping, valves, and alternation to maintain constant circulation and permit lifting water to intended heights comparable to ordinary pumps, with the advantage of remote motive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical construction details and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Receptacles and pipes must be well shut and soldered everywhere; valves must work by springs to keep water from returning; concealed piping should be well soldered where it passes through rock coverings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific assembly guidance: ensure tight sealing to maintain air rarefaction/pressure differentials; conceal and hide pipes (where secrecy or aesthetics require); fit valves to prevent backflow; place pumps in protected locations so they can be worked unseen if necessary. Notes on how opened bellows are aided by external air pressure, assisting the lifting of opposite bellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for extracting and using purple dye from purpura (shell-fish)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: break harder shells with a smart hammer-stroke (mouths downwards) on iron or timber, pick off broken pieces to expose a white vein (next to the head) and dig out that vein with the stiff point of a shortened horse-hair pencil; use the extracted matter to write/tracings on linen or silk, pressing as much as possible with the pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour development: initial marks appear light green, then with sun exposure progress through deep green, sea-green, watchet blue, purplish red to a very deep purple red; fastest in strong sun (times of exposure differ by season/time of day — e.g., winter about noon; summer an hour or two after sunrise). After washing in scalding water and soap and drying in sun/wind the final colour becomes a bright crimson (prince's colour) that will remain if well managed; repeated washing may slightly allay brightness. Storage: keep samples in a book to exclude air (air exposure causes fading of intermediate colours). Sensory note: while drying in sun the cloth yields a fetid smell like garlic/asafcetida. Historical/economic context: Tyrian purple regarded as finest; this species (purpura littoralis) may rival Tyrian purple with improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomic division of fishes by internal/external anatomy and mode of generation
rubrics_metrics.description: General division into three chief kinds: 1) cetaceous (sea-beasts) — generate viviparously like quadrupeds; 2) cartilaginous — inwardly oviparous, breed large eggs (distinction of yolk/white) often hatched in the womb (externally viviparous in practice); 3) spinose — oviparous, cast spawn (numerous small eggs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further morphological subdivisions: cartilaginous into long/round (sharks/dogs) and flat/broad (suborbinate); spinose subdivided by body shape (flat, anguilliform, shorter thick-bodied) and by fin characters (number of dorsal fins; whether rays are soft/flexible or stiff/spinose). The classification relies on many characters: internal/external parts, gills, swimming bladder, fins, reproduction, and observed uses/behaviours; authors present catalogues of local fishes as exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical and physiological inference must be based on dissection and experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims such as gills being 'inverted lungs', the whole mass of blood passing through gills, the necessity of air for fishes' respiration, the swimming-bladder's role in equilibrium, and presence of kidneys/bladders are supported by dissections and experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental evidence examples: breaking the air-bladder causes inability to maintain position (sinks to bottom), showing its role; varied dissections demonstrate that few fishes lack a bladder and none lack kidneys. The text emphasises repeated, undoubted experiments and dissections to settle contested physiological questions (e.g., whether fishes hear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for establishing geographic latitudes and correcting authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely unquestioningly on received latitudes from ancient/medieval authorities (Ptolemy, Appianus, Arabians); instead perform direct astronomical observations (meridian altitude of the sun) with reliable instruments (e.g., brass sextant of large radius or astrolabe) to determine latitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's practice: measured Constantinople with a brass sextant (4-ft radius) at summer solstice and found 41° 6', contradicting Greek (43° 5') and Arabic (45°) authorities; measured Rhodes with a Gemma Frisius astrolabe and found 37° 50'. Recommendation: use such observations to rectify maps and the positions of cities, rather than accepting transmitted geographical tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of inscriptions: use imagery, letter-forms, and comparative alphabets
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpreting runic or ancient inscriptions, consider the material imagery (e.g., depiction of baptism with dove) and letter-forms; compare characters with authoritative corpora (Wormius's Literatura Runica) and other alphabets; note possible mixtures of tongues (Danish, Saxon, British) in border regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overreliance on distant textual vouchers; let the inscription and its iconography speak; be cautious with decayed or defective inscriptions (defects may discourage attempts to expound). Readings should account for local linguistic mixtures and historical population movements (e.g., Danes and Saxons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental reporting of mental-arithmetic/memory demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: For demonstrations testing memory strength: control attentional conditions (e.g., perform operations by night in the dark or with eyes shut to reduce distractions) and provide concrete numerical examples (e.g., square roots extracted to many decimal places).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's account: mental extraction of roots of numbers of many places (8, 10, 12, up to 53 places with root to 27 places) retained until subsequently written by daylight; conclusion: a 'tolerably good memory, fixed with close attention' can hold large amounts. Implies standards for reproducibility: report exact numbers, conditions (dark/night, eyes shut), and retention/recording procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation practice: include specific descriptive detail, figures, and exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide plates/figures (PI. 8 figs. referenced) showing instruments, shell examples, opercula, and model devices; give precise measurements and weights (e.g., stone compass 5-1 inches, length 4-1/2 inches, weight 3 ounces avoirdupois), and step-by-step processes for manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete exemplars, dimensions, named plates/figures, and specific numerical data to allow readers to visualize and reproduce findings or constructions. When describing specimens (shells, stones, inscriptions), report provenance, dates, and any relevant subsequent conditions (e.g., patient had urine incontinence after stone discharge).
